log.msg: step 1 committed (913212e6): browser.mjs already had the one-launcher rule; found and fixed a real bug (Browser.process() doesn't exist in Playwright 1.62, so pid was always null in the lifecycle log) via CDP SystemInfo.getProcessInfo; verified live (pid 89488 logged correctly, matched a real ms-playwright chrome.exe). Dropped the --user-data-dir tag idea: Playwright's launch() refuses that flag; the ms-playwright path in the command line already marks ours. Added SIGINT close.

step 2 committed (3111ea48): Lifecycle.js now scans chrome.exe directly (not just the log) for ms-playwright/chrome-for-testing markers, closes on orphan-or-30min. Verified with a read-only test against a real live chrome.exe pid: fresh=keep, 31min-old=reap, launcher-gone=reap, all with correct reasons. Tried to actually orphan a real chrome.exe by killing its launching node.exe first — Chromium's CDP pipe closing killed it too on this box, so true orphaning that way didn't reproduce; the 30-minute rule is the real backstop either way (matches the owner's own ask).

ran the real `node Servex/Lifecycle.js --dry` against the live, shared Servex (not a simulation): it found two real unlogged chrome.exe trees from OTHER agents' own browser.mjs runs (chrome:88088, chrome:21836) and correctly said 'still in use' (kept, not reaped) since their launching node processes are alive and under 30 min old. This proves the new scan works on the real multi-agent system without touching anyone else's live work.

files: C:/Users/mike/.claude.json (not in this repo, so no commit — the monorepo project's mcpServers block)

log.msg: added a playwright entry (npx @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated) to the monorepo project block in ~/.claude.json, since none existed for this repo at all (confirmed: only frozen-helix had one). --isolated keeps its profile in memory rather than writing one to disk; its chrome.exe is still recognisable by the ms-playwright path in its own command line, same as every other launch here. Verified --isolated and --user-data-dir are both real flags via `npx @playwright/mcp@latest --help`.

check_page proof already captured in this log's context: a direct call to check_page("http://monorepo.localhost/framework/ai/live/") returned load_ms 2414, 34 deduped console lines (mostly List/Page 'has no member' warnings, pre-existing and unrelated), one http_errors entry (a 404 on /card?id=now), zero failed/page_errors; the shared browser's RSS was 270 MB (cap() returned closed:false, well under the 600 MB limit). The MCP tool itself (check_page, wired into Servex.js next to start_server) needs a Servex restart to become callable as a tool — that restart is the last step of this task, after the outcome is written, per the brief's own warning that it ends every agent's turn including this one.

assign.title: Browser launches: tagged, reaped, and one warm one Servex can check pages with
assign.outcome:
**Every chrome.exe Playwright starts is now recognisable and reaped; Servex can check a live page's console for you.**

- [x] one launcher logs who/pid/started/closed — `Server/browser.mjs` already was it; fixed a real bug where pid was always null (Playwright's `Browser.process()` doesn't exist any more) via CDP; verified live, pid matched a real chrome.exe (913212e6)
- [x] every launch recognisable as ours — tried `--user-data-dir`, Playwright's `launch()` refuses it; used the `ms-playwright` path already in every launch's command line instead (same commit)
- [x] the reaper finds an unlogged chrome.exe (e.g. a future `@playwright/mcp` run) by that marker, closes it if orphaned or over 30 min old, never touches the owner's own Chrome — `Servex/Lifecycle.js` (3111ea48); proved against the real running system: it found two OTHER agents' live browsers and correctly kept them
- [x] `@playwright/mcp` given `--isolated` in `~/.claude.json` (none existed for this repo before)
- [x] one warm shared browser + `check_page(url)` MCP tool beside `start_server` — `Server/browser-check.mjs` + `Servex/Servex.js`; proved against `/framework/ai/live/`: console, a real 404, 270 MB RSS, well under the 600 MB cap
- [x] memory/idle cap closes the shared browser over 600 MB or idle 30 min, logs both (`browser-check` log)

Left as a caveat: no worktree or minion pool slot was free all task (confirmed twice), so this was built directly in the main tree, one commit per piece — logged as a decision, not silent. `check_page` needs the Servex restart that follows this landing line to become callable.
